advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the inspect.getsource() source-grep in test_cli_search_ready_gate_on_store_is_usable with a behavioral assertion (or drop it, since the four behavioral tests already verify both arms reject unusable stores and accept a valid-empty store).
evidence: reads_cli.py is executable source under test, not a non-executable instruction artifact, so the Rule-5 structural-artifact exception does not apply; a refactor that gates via a helper (e.g. `_require_usable(tracker)`) or an aliased predicate would preserve observable behavior yet fail this test, satisfying the Rule-4 refactoring-violation criterion.

The observable contract is already fully verified by the four behavioral parametrized tests (absent/broken/mid-clone/valid-empty), so this structural grep adds only refactor coupling, not regression protection.
advisory.finding: test_cli_search_ready_gate_on_store_is_usable asserts on the text of the implementation via inspect.getsource(arm), requiring the literal 'store_is_usable(tracker)' substring and forbidding 'os.path.isdir(tracker)' in the source of _cmd_search/_cmd_ready. This is source-grepping the code under test — a change-detector that breaks on a behavior-preserving refactor (e.g. extracting the gate into a shared helper or aliasing the predicate) with no observable-behavior change.
scenarios: A future refactor factors the shared readiness gate into a helper `_require_usable(tracker)` called by both arms; observable behavior (rc 1 / rc 0) is unchanged but this test fails.
The predicate is imported under an alias or invoked through an indirection; the literal substring disappears though behavior is identical.
advisory.suggested_fix: Remove test_cli_search_ready_gate_on_store_is_usable; its intent (both arms gate on usability) is already covered behaviorally by the parametrized reject/accept tests. If parity coverage of a newly added arm is desired, enforce it by enumerating read arms in a table the behavioral parametrization iterates, not by grepping source text.
